_comment_overview: Config for modules/decision_frame.py: evidence -> candidates -> scoring, on top of the rule table in recommendations.json. Signal processing and scoring plumbing, not a vehicle-dynamics method. Every number states its provenance grade -- placeholders are marked as such.

intervention_evidence._comment: ABS/TC evidence, one flag per source. ABS on (trusted position channel log_abs_pos); TC and EB off until their channel identity is mapped. ABS bridge confidence 0.8, not 1.0 -- single-session sensor semantics, revisit.

abs.confidence_derived_from: Deepening Phase 4c (2026-09-18), user decision -- 'sensor boolean, single-session semantics, revisit'. Supersedes Stage 2's own autonomous confidence=1.0 default for this same evidence.

abs_inactive_corroborates_braking_instab._comment: Engineer rule: 'instability/locking under braking + ABS not intervening -> ABS map up'. Fires when abs_active is 0 over the WHOLE entry_1_brake window of a lap AND the corner has unstable_yaw matrix-verdict evidence there. Current log_abs_pos goes into the source text only -- positions are non-monotonic, nothing to route on. Corroborating only, never its own action.

abs_heavy_masks_verdict._comment: Engineer rule: 'ABS regulating heavily through braking zones -> flag as masking, prefer brake-balance/platform levers'. Fires when abs_active duty cycle in entry_1_brake > heavy_duty_cycle_threshold. A flag (masked_by_heavy_abs), not verdict evidence: the braking-phase reading may be ABS regulation, not mechanical balance. Never creates an action.
abs_heavy_masks_verdict.heavy_duty_cycle_threshold_derived_from: ROUND number, NOT gap-selected -- only 5 real per-instance ABS duty-cycle observations exist on GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt (range 26%-57%, too few for a robust gap), Deepening Phase 4c census. 0.5 (more than half the braking phase under ABS regulation) is deliberately conservative/rare -- only 1 of the 5 observed instances would qualify -- revisit once more sessions provide a real distribution to gap-select against.

tc.confidence_note: Unchanged from Stage 2 -- TC stays dormant (Deepening Phase 4c, user decision: 'TC/EB stay dormant pending mapping'), so this confidence value is not yet load-bearing either way.

tc_active_corroborates_traction_limited._comment: Fires when ecu_B_tc_act is 1 anywhere in exit_4/exit_5 of a lap AND the corner/phase has oversteer matrix-verdict evidence. Corroborates traction_limited (or stands alone where LS is invalid). Evidence only, never an action.

plausibility_checks._comment: Cheap checks, generated whenever their evidence fires. Data checks against config bounds, not vehicle-dynamics claims.

tyre_pressure_window._comment: Per-axle hot-pressure window. No source for it anywhere in the repo -> null on purpose rather than a guessed limit.
tyre_pressure_window.derived_from: NEEDS USER INPUT -- no target hot-pressure window exists anywhere in this project's config or docs. Supply front/rear (or per-corner) min/max in psi from tyre data sheet or team practice before this check can ever fire; until then it is wired but permanently silent (no evidence, not a false negative). CHANNEL-CENSUS CORRECTION 2026-09-22 (DECISION LAYER SPEC Phase A5): the claim above ('zero tyre-pressure entries anywhere') was checked only against config/channels.json, config/parameters.json, config/setup_parameters.json, config/car_data.json -- it was never checked against the raw telemetry files themselves, which the channel census rule requires. Direct census of both real sessions found tpms_press_fl/fr/rl/rr[bar] (plus _abs/_raw/_dash variants) IS present and populated on both Sample_Dubai.txt and GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt, 1 Hz, real varying values (~1.6-1.8 bar plausible range) alongside clear startup/dropout glitches (Dubai: 20.47 bar spike at channel start; v3: 6.2 bar at start, an isolated 296.7 bar dropout spike) that would need a Tier B exclusion mask before any production use. This corrects the earlier premise, not the target-window gap: the LIVE CHANNEL exists, but the TARGET pressure (this file's own min/max here and in tyre_pressure_target below) still does not -- no data sheet or team-practice number exists anywhere in this repo, so both blocks stay null on purpose, unchanged in effect. No production wiring done this session (out of Phase A's own scope).

brake_balance_signature._comment: Front axle past its limit while the rear stays healthy under braking. Uses classify_fn's severity labels, not raw CS numbers -- the classification thresholds are never duplicated here.
brake_balance_signature.derived_from: Tier B. 'Beyond limit' = front axle's classify_fn severity on entry_1_brake reaches front_beyond_severity_min (today: 'moderate', i.e. CS_ratio_f at or past config/parameters.json classification.MODERATE_CSF). 'Healthy' = rear axle's severity on the same phase stays at/below rear_healthy_severity_max (today: 'normal', i.e. rear CS_ratio_r has not crossed even MODERATE_CSR). Reuses the existing _phase_verdict/classify_fn path (modules/recommendation.py) unmodified, per-axle -- guarantees this check can never disagree with what the stability grid already shows for the same corner/phase.

_comment_tyre_pressure_target: Tyre pressures are never recommended, only flagged beside the shortlist when out of window, on the apex-window median only (apex = peak lateral load; author decision 2026-09-28). Per corner, with a compound note. Replaces plausibility_checks.tyre_pressure_window for the decision frame. tpms_press_* is a measurement, not a target -- no target exists, so all null.

tyre_pressure_target._comment_units: Units are bar (min_bar/max_bar), like the tpms_press_* channels -- the earlier psi names were wrong (docs/channel_requirements.md; diagnostics/inspect_tpms_pressure_cornering_phase.py).
tyre_pressure_target.location_all_but_max_in_band_derived_fro: Author 2026-09-28 (display): when this many corners or fewer sit IN band, an off-band wheel is written "all but C.../C..." instead of the positive corner list.
tyre_pressure_target.compound_note: Author-elicited 2026-09-24: this band is COMPOUND-SCOPED, not universal -- it assumes one specific tyre compound. The tool has no per-outing compound field or channel (verified: neither exists anywhere in this codebase), so it cannot detect or auto-suppress a session run on a different compound. A session whose apex pressure sits consistently and uniformly below/above this band on all four corners may simply be a different compound, not a real pressure problem -- read this note before acting on a flag. A per-outing compound field is a named future refinement, not built here.
tyre_pressure_target.derived_from: Author-elicited 2026-09-24 (WP-ELICIT Phase B2, elicitation item 2 RESOLVED): front 1.85-1.95 bar, rear 1.80-1.90 bar; per-corner fields inherit their axle's band (fl/fr share the front band, rl/rr share the rear band -- no per-corner distinction elicited). Verified live before activating (channel census rule): tpms_press_fl/fr/rl/rr confirmed present, unit bar, real cornering-phase variation on both sessions (diagnostics/inspect_tpms_pressure_cornering_phase.py, thesis_notes.md) -- channel identity/semantics check out; v3's cornering-phase readings sit near/inside this band, Dubai's sit consistently below it (see compound_note above for why that is not treated as a pressure fault).

_comment_scoring_weights_retired: scoring_weights retired -- everything lives in cost_function: severity_weight/phase_importance -> severity/phase_importance (problem weight); effect_weight/effect_class_multiplier -> effect_class (lever fit, not problem weight); effort_weight -> change_time; settings_window_weight -> headroom; interaction_weight -> interaction; confidence_weight folded into the problem-weight product. score() reads cost_function only.

driver_feedback_weighting._comment: Confidence of a driver_feedback evidence item (corroborates an existing candidate at the same corner/phase/verdict, via min confidence; never its own candidate). Step function over |raw feedback| in three bands matching the scale: |1| slight, |3| strong, |5| undrivable. The shape is fixed; band values provisional (see derived_from).

ls_threshold_evidence._comment: LS thresholds, phase-scoped, kept here on purpose -- not in parameters.json classification, so they can never become a verdict tier or severity colour. Read by _build_ls_threshold_evidence. Derived from 71 negative worst-phase instances on both sessions, checked against brake/throttle/ABS/TC/|ax|/repeatability.
ls_threshold_evidence.STRONG_LSF_derived_from: LS-evidence census pooled p10 (front), same physical anchor logic as CS_ratio's own STRONG_CSF/CSR (0 = the ratio's own peak-force point, minus a data-sized margin) -- Metrology extension Phase 2's own repaired-estimator distribution, n=31 pooled corners. Reopen condition: a validity-repair-scale re-derivation if a third session's own distribution shifts this materially; small-n caveat carried over unchanged from the original proposal.
ls_threshold_evidence.STRONG_LSR_derived_from: Same population/method as STRONG_LSF, rear axle pooled p10. Reopen condition identical.
ls_threshold_evidence.exit_phase_confidence_discount_derived_f: LS-evidence census, 2026-09-20: exit-phase negative instances corroborate at only 34% (15/44) vs braking 89% (8/9) and turn-in/apex 72% (13/18) -- the discriminating factor is NAMED, not just observed: TC (the natural exit/traction corroborator) fires on only 3 samples in v3's entire session (0.0044%, thesis_notes.md 'Frame-Stage-2 Phase 2: intervention-channel survey'), so exit-phase readings are structurally unable to be TC-corroborated this session regardless of whether the underlying signal is real -- an evidence gap, not a demonstrated absence of signal. 0.5 reuses intervention_evidence.abs.confidence's own 0.8-cap PRECEDENT (a MIN-confidence ceiling, not a new discount mechanism) at a value matching this source's own weaker (34%, vs ABS's 41.92% co-occurrence) corroboration rate. Applied via min() against the SAME repeat-fraction confidence _build_corner_verdict_evidence already computes -- repeatability across a corner's own laps (the Dubai C3 pattern: exit_5 rear, repeat=4/4, corroborated via repeatability alone with zero TC activity) is what lifts a reading UP TO this ceiling rather than leaving it at a low one-off fraction; min() cannot inflate a genuinely low fraction past what it already is. REOPEN CONDITION, stated explicitly per the work order: a session with real, non-trivial TC activity re-derives this discount (or removes the need for it) by closing the evidence gap directly instead of working around it.

_comment_parameter_windows: One entry per registry key (46). nominal + span from the registry's typical_window/value_space: span = half the typical window width (one-sided, e.g. arb_fl 4 +/- 1 from 3..5); no typical window -> nominal = value_space midpoint, span = half the legal range (wider, weaker, flagged). Plain enums without an underlying number stay null (arb_front_mount, wing_position). Null window or non-numeric current value -> neutral headroom term.

_comment_interaction_table: Signed side effects per (parameter, direction, axis). Matrix-derived: every parameter used by another rule in the same direction for a different axis (+1) or the opposite direction (-1) -- arb_fl/fr/rl/rr, camber_fl/fr, diff_position, ride_height_front/rear, tc_lon, toe_front. Left out: abs_position (categorical), tc_lat and the 20 damper keys (one rule each, nothing to cross-reference), wing_position ('increase' fixes both understeer and oversteer by phase), dead front_arb/rear_arb names. springs_front/rear: literature entries (Segers ch. 9/10) -- front/rear roll-stiffness split moves balance; spring rate also moves the platform, ARB doesn't. Total lateral transfer is fixed by geometry/CoG, only its split is tunable -> no 'total grip' axis. grade: 'derived-from-matrix', 'proposed' or 'proposed (Segers ch.9/10)' -- all proposed grades advisory-capped.
_comment_performance_axes: Axis vocabulary: understeer_tendency, oversteer_tendency (two axes, not one bipolar scale), yaw_stability, braking_performance, traction_performance, platform_stability (Segers ch. 9/10). Matched against the verdict type of the corner's other active problems. Only the first three map to a verdict (_AXIS_TO_VERDICT); the rest are inert until an evidence source exists.

_comment_cost_function: Six scoring terms, nothing outside this block: (1) problem weight = severity x sev_rank x phase_importance x confidence; (2) change_time (inverse effort -- track time is scarce); (3) breadth (global lever helping 1 of N, see breadth_derived_from); (4) headroom (settings-window distance); (5) interaction; (6) effect_class (lever fit, primary vs secondary -- not part of problem weight: one problem, different effect classes per lever). severity/change_time shape elicited: one change at a time, 45-50 min session rhythm -> change_time dominates, severity orders within an effort class and only overrides past the heavy-corrector gate. Terms are additive, so a weight's neutral value is 0.0. breadth 0.0 (annotation-only), headroom/interaction 0.1 each (joint 0.2 < 0.2083, the smallest change_time class step), effect_class 1.0/0.6 -- all author-elicited 2026-09-26; phase_importance ordering elicited.

cost_function.change_time_derived_from: Per-class table, author-elicited 2026-09-28: "electronic mitigation like TC still costs lap time (cutting power); the mechanical fix adds grip -- halve the while-driving favor." Seconds 2.5 -> 1.875, so the seconds-minutes gap halves (1.25 -> 0.625); minutes/half_hour/garage_hours keep their former values (2.5/(rank+1): 1.25, 0.8333, 0.625), so the smallest class step stays 0.2083 and the headroom+interaction joint bound 0.2 still clears it. Intended consequence: at exit a strong-problem minutes fix now outranks a moderate-problem seconds fix. Earlier record: Author-elicited 2026-09-24 (WP-ELICIT Phase A1, elicitation item 1, PARTIAL -- severity/change_time shape only). Sized against severity=1.0 so the two constructed proofs both hold at typical phase_importance/confidence (exit_4, pi=1.2, confidence=1.0): (a) a click-class fix for a MODERATE problem outranks a heavy-corrector fix one severity rank up (garage_hours effort) -- normal-case change_time dominance; (b) a heavy corrector at STRONG severity with full breadth/primary effect_class still beats a NORMAL-severity click-class distractor -- severity punches through only across the FULL normal->strong range, i.e. at the eligibility gate's own ceiling, never merely one rank up. See tests/test_decision_frame.py term-order tests for the exact constructed proofs; thesis_notes.md 'WP-ELICIT Phase A' for the full derivation.
cost_function.breadth_derived_from: author-elicited 2026-09-26: deliberately neutral, annotation-only -- the 'helps X, risks others' dropdown line carries the caution; the real gate for lonely-corner problems is driver corroboration (no complaint + single corner = no change; the existing 0.5 no-corroboration confidence cap implements this). Weight 0.0 = annotation-only in the additive score: the breadth_note line stays shown, the term adds nothing. Formula kept (inert at weight 0.0), Tier B (Stage 6 names the CONCEPT -- 'global lever helping 1 of N corners is penalised' -- not a formula): penalty = -(1 - corners_helped/corners_touched) when breadth data is available and the lever is not exempt (0 when exempt -- corners_touched==corners_helped by construction, modules/decision_frame.py _attach_breadth; 0, flagged, when assessed_corner_ids was not supplied to generate_candidates at all). Fraction-based, clamped at 0 when the candidate helps every assessed corner -- same normalized-distance style this file's own _settings_window_component formula already uses ('1 - distance/span'), not a new invented style.
cost_function.headroom_derived_from: author-elicited 2026-09-26: near a physical limit, prefer the lever with more room -- 'stay inside its comfort range'; weaker than change_time, decides between comparable-effort options only. Term = headroom x (1 - |new - nominal|/span, clipped), so it adds between 0 (window edge) and 0.1 (nominal); neutral 0 where no window or no setup value exists. Bound from the live arithmetic: change_time = 2.5/(effort_rank+1) gives class steps 1.25 / 0.4167 / 0.2083; the smallest is 0.2083 (half_hour -> garage_hours). Joint bound with interaction: 0.1 + 0.1 = 0.2 < 0.2083, so headroom and interaction together can never flip adjacent effort classes.

Same joint bound as headroom: 0.1 + 0.1 = 0.2 < 0.2083, the smallest change_time class step; the once-only count is what keeps the bound true for axle packages.

conditions.not_evaluable_confidence_cap_derived_fro: Reuses ls_threshold_evidence.exit_phase_confidence_discount's own 0.5 PRECEDENT (2026-09-20) -- not a new number invented for this mechanism. Same justification transfers directly: an evidence gap (there, exit-phase TC corroboration being structurally unavailable this session; here, any not-evaluable condition -- missing evidence source, unfilled setup sheet, missing registry window) caps confidence via min() rather than suppressing the candidate outright, at a value already established in this same config file for exactly this kind of gap. Applied via the SAME min()-confidence mechanism every other cap in this file uses (MARGINAL-verdict cap, exit-phase LS discount, ABS-masking) -- min() can only ever LOWER a candidate's confidence, never raise it, so a candidate whose OWN evidence already reports confidence below 0.5 is untouched (never inflated up to the cap).

Wired only for evidence types that exist today (damper_motion: modules/damper_motion.py; intervention_abs/intervention_tc: Stage 2 Phase 3c) -- 'lockup' is listed as a deliberate placeholder for docs/segers_bridge_review.md's own reviewed C5-2 lockup-evidence proposal, not yet built (PLAN.md FRAME DEPTH PROGRAMME Step 5); it can never match today (no evidence item of type 'lockup' is ever produced), by design, per the work order's own 'wire only those that exist today... leave the list config-driven and extensible' instruction. _comment_damper_motion: Damper motion evidence (damper_motion.py): loading/unloading per corner, transient phase (entry/exit, never apex -- Segers ch. 11) and wheel, from log_susp_travel_*. Sign checked on both sessions: corr(front travel, braking ax) +0.49 Dubai, +0.20 v3 -> decreasing travel = compression = loading. Threshold reference population = straight-line mask (|ax| < 0.5, |ay| < 0.5 g); apex_3 segments too short to use.

damper_motion.rate_threshold_mm_s_derived_from: Pooled straight-line (|ax|<0.5,|ay|<0.5 g, kerb-excluded) |travel rate| median across both real sessions and all non-dead wheels: 0.975 mm/s (n=1830, Dubai 510 windows p50=0.825, v3 1320 windows p50=1.061) -- rounded to a clean 1.0 mm/s just above it. This is NOT a clean bimodal gap (the straight-line population's own upper tail, p90=4.67/p95=6.68 mm/s, genuinely overlaps the transient population's own median, 1.87 mm/s pooled -- real road-texture/engine-vibration chassis motion exists even on a straight, this is not pure sensor noise) -- the median of the 'nothing deliberately dynamic happening' reference population is the honest, data-grounded choice available, not a cleanly-separated threshold; revisit if a future session's own distribution suggests otherwise. diagnostics/inspect_damper_motion_sign_and_threshold.py, thesis_notes.md.
